job: Rewriting the MCP/tool-execution boundary so agent-invoked tools run containerized with dropped host privileges instead of trust-the-authenticated-user, run-on-the-host.
outcome: A released framework version where sandboxed, least-privilege MCP tool execution is the shipped default rather than an opt-in configuration flag.
motivation: The late-June CVE cluster made host-privileged tool execution a reputational and CVSS-9.9 liability the project cannot keep shipping as default behavior.

task.who: Core runtime and security engineering maintainers
task.what: Containerize tool runners and drop host privileges by default
task.when: Across the next two release cycles through Q1 2027
task.why: Foreclose the shared authenticated-user-to-host RCE failure mode
task.how: Container isolation plus allowlist command validation replacing blocklists

actor: Agentic-AI security researcher and CVE reporter
job: Disclosing and scoring command-injection and code-execution flaws at the tool boundary, keeping pressure on maintainers to harden execution defaults.
outcome: A steady stream of high-severity advisories that make opt-in sandboxing untenable and push frameworks to adopt secure-by-default tool execution.
motivation: Recurring critical RCE at the same trust boundary shows the class is systemic, and researchers gain credibility by forcing the ecosystem fix.

task.what: Find and disclose tool-boundary command-injection and RCE flaws
task.where: Agent-builder codebases and their MCP tool runners
task.when: Continuously through the two-release-cycle runway to Q1 2027
task.why: Sustain pressure until sandboxed defaults ship across frameworks
